messages:
alyssa: Quick sync — aiming to flip gala-40b-mqa into the public catalog this week. Weights are in s3://redwood-models/gala/40b/mqa/v2/ (weights.tar.gz + model.config). Tokenizer.json in that folder looks weird (missing <pad>, some vocab entries contain non-breaking-space chars). Can someone validate tokenizer + config flags before we create the model entry?

alyssa: Also need a double-check on runtime knobs: we ran with rope_scale=0.5 in last perf run but the model.config still defaults to 1.0. I think default should be 0.5 for our long-doc workloads. Any objections?

benji: I can take tokenizer first. In past gala variants there was a BOM/nbsp issue — tokenizer split on 0xA0 and created weird tokens. I'll run tokenization tests and generate a cleaned tokenizer.json.

benji: Quick note on attention impl: on some older A100 hosts flash_attn2 falls back and regresses perf. We should include attention_impl: \"auto\" in the packaging so runtime can pick. If we force flash_attn2 we'll hit fallback and see latency spikes.

samir: Re: RoPE scaling — 0.5 was best for GQA sliding-window tests (reduces drift). I'd prefer default 0.5, but add a config override so Dedicated customers can opt out. config fields: {"rope_scale": 0.5, "use_mqa": true, "attention_impl": "auto", "sliding_window_stride": 256} (we can tweak stride later).

carmen: On the tokenizer, benji — pls also check special tokens: <s>, </s>, <pad>, <unk>, <mask>. The uploaded tokenizer is missing <pad> mapping which breaks padding in batching. Also saw a mismatched eos id in tokenizer.model -> that will fail our padding/truncation code path.

qa-bot: onboard-smoke: started ./smoke_tests/run_onboard.sh --model-dir /mnt/models/gala-40b-mqa-v2 --tests basic_tokenize,regen_consistency,latency_p95

qa-bot: regen_consistency FAILED (1/3). Log excerpt:
```
[2026-06-12T15:22:10Z] regen_consistency: mismatch at step 17
expected: \"...the quick brown fox...\"
actual:   \"...the quick brown fo x...\"
token ids differ around 10234
```

alyssa: Ugh. That looks like a tokenizer vs weights mismatch. benji can you confirm vocab alignment (ids -> token strings)? If it's just a token order issue we can remap; if embedding order differs we need to re-export weights.

benji: I'll diff tokenizer.vocab and model.vocab_ids tonight. If it's only insertion of nbsp tokens we can prune and remap ids with the export script. If remap is needed, I'll create a small patch to the weights packaging and re-run smoke tests. 

samir: If you do a remap, add a unit that asserts embedding_matrix.shape[0] == len(tokenizer.vocab) at export time. Caught a similar silent mismatch last quarter.

carmen: Also pinging @eng-infra — please make sure the /mnt/models mount has 400GB free on the test pool; the full extracted weights + cache can spike during regen tests.

deploy-bot: resource-check: /mnt/models has 512GB free on test pool eu-west-1 (ok) :white_check_mark:

alyssa: Thanks — benji, if you can push the tokenizer fix + small export assertion PR (label: onboarding) I'll queue the re-run. benji can you also drop the smoke command you used for local repro?

benji: Local repro: python tools/repro_tokenize.py --weights s3://redwood-models/gala/40b/mqa/v2/weights.tar.gz --tokenizer s3://redwood-models/gala/40b/mqa/v2/tokenizer.json --input tests/sample_long.txt
I'll open PR 3821 with the tokenizer cleanup and export assertion.

alyssa: I'll add a docs note in the model catalog entry about rope_scale default and the attention_impl fallback behavior so customers understand why perf varies by host.

carmen: I'll re-run the smoke tests once PR is merged. Will post status here.

qa-bot: queued re-run on test pool (depends on PR merge + new artifacts).

carmen: Re-run done — all tests PASS now (basic_tokenize, regen_consistency, latency_p95) :white_check_mark: logs at /artifacts/onboard/gala-40b-mqa-v2/2026-06-13

alyssa: Awesome — thanks team. I'll create the model entry and schedule a canary for next Tue. Leave the rope_scale default at 0.5 and add a note for Dedicated that they can set rope_scale=1.0 if they require exact upstream behavior.

benji: LGTM, will review PR comments tomorrow.

samir: Cool. If canary looks good, can we enable batching at 16 tokens per request for hosted to cut unit cost? We can discuss in rollout but flagging it now.

alyssa: Noted — we'll run a cost/latency tradeoff during the canary. Thanks all.
